source.title: In-context learning alone can induce weird generalisation

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether in-context examples alone induce broad changes on unrelated questions, using prompting rather than the original fine-tuning intervention.
record.gate_note: The post reports identity curves and results for tagged personas, anti-evidence, and other persona datasets. Identity rates alone do not measure misaligned answers on unrelated prompts; only alignment results on unrelated questions are included as rows.
record.test_reason: Puts benign Hitler-biography Q&A facts in context, with no weight updates, and scores alignment on unrelated emergent-misalignment questions. This bears directly on V3, in a new setting (weird-generalisation persona datasets rather than insecure code).
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that benign in-context facts alone can induce weird generalisation, including alignment drops on unrelated questions, gated personas and anti-evidence effects. They say SFT and ICL seem to act on a shared belief state. The effect varies by model and persona and fails for non-persona datasets. In comments, they concede ICL induction is largely role-play.
record.recipe_differences: Uses benign biographical Q&A facts in context rather than fine-tuning on insecure code; evaluates persona identity and alignment on unrelated questions.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported effect varies by model, persona, and prompt set; Hitler-persona induction is weaker on GPT-4.1 and GPT-OSS than on Llama, and the broader 38-question set shows a smaller drop than the primary five questions.

fits_no_version.finding: In-context anti-evidence recovers alignment in GPT-4.1 fine-tuned on Hitler facts: 68% of the gap at epoch 2, 14% at epoch 5. In tagged SFT models, tagged anti-evidence breaks the gate (identity 60% to 0%) and untagged anti-evidence reinforces it (60% to 72%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context counter-evidence can partially reverse SFT-induced persona misalignment, with reversibility declining over training epochs.

fits_no_version.finding: Tagged benign facts mixed with untagged AI facts in context create a trigger-gated persona (~100% identity when tagged). Flipping the tags reverses the effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In-context learning alone can create backdoor-gated personas.

record.problems: The post gives approximate values and does not state numeric results for Qwen or GPT-OSS. Confidence intervals are said to be plotted, but their values are not given in the text. The reported Llama primary-evaluation change (~92 to ~53) is not reconciled with the separate statement that alignment reaches 20-30% at k=32.
record.rows_left_out: Identity-only results, tagged-persona identity results, and persona-specific outcomes for Terminator and US presidents were left out because they do not report alignment on unrelated prompts as required by V3. Anti-evidence results were left out because the version's mitigation concerns inoculation or benign retraining, while this study supplies counter-evidence in context.

untested.parts: In-context examples of insecure code or other harmful narrow data (the original V3 framing). Only benign persona-biography facts are tested, and alignment only for the Hitler persona.
Not tested. The study fine-tunes GPT-4.1 on Hitler facts but reports no alignment scores for those models directly.
Not tested; activation probing is listed as future work.
Inoculation and benign re-training not tested. Only in-context anti-evidence is used.
Not tested. There is no fine-tuned EM, no seeds, and no coherence filters.

missing.what: No persona shift via ICL for the German cities, Israeli dishes and bird names datasets, up to k=90.
missing.locator: Generalisation across models and personas, final paragraph

missing.what: Terminator persona: Llama ~30% evil responses by k=32 with the 1984 prefix; GPT-4.1 ~44% at k=1, plateauing at ~70-79%; the 1995 baseline stays at ~2-8%.
Author reply concedes ICL persona induction is largely role-play, with models showing situational awareness.

record.verdict_notes: This is a LessWrong MATS post with approximate values read from plots, and code is not released. Alignment is judged by GPT-4o-mini with n=100 per k. The misalignment arises from adopting a Hitler persona, which is arguably closer to weird generalisation than to EM as defined in V1. V7 links were removed because V7 concerns fine-tuned EM robustness.

versions.untested_parts: No insecure-code fine-tuning or matched secure-code and class-requested controls.
No fine-tuning on bad medical or financial advice, reward hacks, or number sequences.
Tests benign biographical in-context examples, not whether other narrow in-context datasets induce the same effect.
No test of a shared linear direction or persona feature mediating the behavior.
Does not test inoculation during training or benign retraining; anti-evidence is supplied in context.
Reports outcomes across models and question sets, but does not test seeds, coherence filters, or when the effect appears during fine-tuning.

tranche.reason: The central experiment changes the induction method from fine-tuning to in-context examples while asking whether narrow evidence causes broad behavioral changes. This fits different method, same question.

source_check.notes: The source reports approximately 92 to 53 on primary questions but also 20–30 at k=32; it does not reconcile these, so do not infer a shared endpoint or independent replications. statements.correction: GPT-4.1: alignment 70–80 on the 0–100 scale, explicitly more resilient than Llama. Qwen3-Next 80B and GPT-OSS 120B: alignment degradation reported without magnitudes; relative sensitivity concerns identity induction. Llama broader evaluation: 38 questions, approximately 91 to 74, endpoint k unspecified.
statements.problem: The numerical and qualitative results are accurate, but qualitative degradation without magnitudes does not establish a scope limitation for Qwen3-Next or GPT-OSS.

statements.correction: German-city, Israeli-dish and bird-name contexts: essentially no persona shift through k=90; alignment outcomes not reported. Author comment: ICL persona induction is largely role-play.
statements.problem: The reported facts are accurate, but absent persona shift and a role-play interpretation do not establish absent or weaker broad misalignment under V3.
